"""Delimited-field splitting."""

from __future__ import annotations


def split_fields(line: str, sep: str = ",") -> list[str]:
    """Split one delimited line into its fields.

    Fields are returned exactly as written: surrounding whitespace is kept, an
    empty input yields a single empty field, and a trailing separator yields a
    trailing empty field.

    A field is double-quoted only if its first character is ``"``. Inside a
    quoted field the separator is an ordinary character and two consecutive
    quotes ``""`` stand for one literal ``"``. The enclosing quotes are not
    part of the returned value (so ``""`` is an empty string). After a closing
    quote, the next character must be the separator or the end of the line.
    Quotes that do not start a field are ordinary characters.

    Args:
        line: A single line of delimited text.
        sep: Field separator. Must be exactly one character.

    Returns:
        The fields, in order.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If ``sep`` is not exactly one character, if a quoted field
            is missing its closing quote, or if a character other than ``sep``
            or end-of-line follows a closing quote.
    """
    if len(sep) != 1:
        raise ValueError("sep must be a single character")

    fields: list[str] = []
    n = len(line)
    i = 0

    while True:
        if i < n and line[i] == '"':
            # Quoted field: ends at the closing quote (not preceded as an
            # escape), with "" inside standing for one literal ".
            i += 1
            parts: list[str] = []
            closed = False
            while i < n:
                if line[i] == '"':
                    if i + 1 < n and line[i + 1] == '"':
                        parts.append('"')
                        i += 2
                    else:
                        closed = True
                        i += 1
                        break
                else:
                    parts.append(line[i])
